name: Carlisle Syrah Rosella's Vineyard 2016
text:
## Carlisle Syrah Rosella's Vineyard 2016

**The story.** Carlisle is the story of a home winemaker who went pro. The founder was hooked on wine at 19, when his sister poured him a late-harvest Riesling ("Ambrosia!"). After three years in software development, he started making five gallons of Zinfandel in his kitchen, then a barrel a year with friends and his wife, Kendall Carlisle. They moved to Santa Rosa in [Sonoma County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonoma_County_wine), fell for its ancient, twisted old vines, and by 1997 were making over 300 cases of "garage" wine and winning gold medals in amateur competitions. In 1998, with meagre savings and family support, they launched Carlisle Winery & Vineyards, focusing on old-vine [Zinfandel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zinfandel) and red Rhône varieties: Syrah, Grenache, Mourvèdre and Petite Sirah. Their Zinfandel sources include vineyards planted between 1888 and 1934, including their own, planted in 1927 by Alcide Pelletti ([Carlisle](https://www.carlislewinery.net/our-story)).

**The vineyard: Rosella's.** Rosella's Vineyard lies on the south-east-facing slopes of the mountains separating the Pacific from the [Salinas Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salinas_Valley) in [Monterey County](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Rosella's+Vineyard,+Santa+Lucia+Highlands,+California,+USA&t=k). Carlisle calls it one of California's "grand cru" vineyards: foggy mornings, strong afternoon sea winds and good sun give a long growing season, and in the hands of grower-owner Gary Franscioni it gives [Syrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah) "of uncommon complexity, with notes of ruby-red grapefruit and white pepper" ([Carlisle](https://www.carlislewinery.net/rosellas)).

**The vintage.** Jancis Robinson's [northern California chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/northern-california) describes 2016 as a year of even temperatures and a slightly cooler September that eased harvest pressure, with "a good combination of elegance and structure especially in red varieties"; mid-October rain troubled some late-ripening varieties. Her chart covers the North Coast rather than Monterey, so take it as a general guide.

**What the critics say for 2016.**
- I couldn't find a published critic's note for the 2016 on pages I could read, so I've left critics out rather than guess.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 92.5** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is ten years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2021 to 2031. So it is in its prime: dark fruit with grapefruit, white pepper and savoury notes. Decant an hour ahead and serve at 16°C.

**Food.** Peppery cool-climate Syrah suits grilled lamb, venison, duck, or a steak au poivre.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Carlisle at the moment.

**Curious details**
- **From software to Syrah.** The founder left a software career because he wanted work he was truly passionate about, using his analytical skills creatively ([Carlisle](https://www.carlislewinery.net/our-story)).
- **Kitchen beginnings.** Carlisle's first wine was five gallons of Zinfandel made in a kitchen ([Carlisle](https://www.carlislewinery.net/our-story)).
